display.title: Episode 24: The Whispering Droplets (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi teaches why we count the days of Sefirah and how precious time is, then tells how dripping water convinced Rabbi Akiva that it is never too late to learn Torah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Sefiras HaOmer, the week before Shabbos Mevarchim Sivan. Uncle Yossi explains that counting the Omer teaches how precious each day is: every day should be better than the one before, and time lost never comes back, as a little girl who keeps crying over her lost dime learns from her mother. He looks ahead to the new Chumash, Bamidbar, and calls the Torah a living lesson. A nine-year-old yeshiva boy leads the Shema in Studio 604. The story, 'Never Too Late', tells how Rachel begged her forty-year-old husband Akiva to learn Torah. Sitting by a river, he sees soft drops of water that have bored a hole through hard rock, and realizes that the gentle words of Torah can enter even a hard heart. He becomes the great Rabbi Akiva and gives all the honor to his wife. After a sponsor message, a listener's poem about Moshiach is read, and Uncle Yossi offers a free bonus tape with his story series.
display.lesson: It is never too late to begin learning Torah; time is a precious gift from Hashem, so fill every day with Torah and mitzvos.
